clue.text: Queen dressed appropriately for crowd?

definitions.note: verb: to crowd is to squash together

indicators.note: to be dressed is to be wrapped in clothing, so one piece goes inside a garment

blocks.note: Qu. is a dictionary abbreviation for queen
the fitting garment for a queen is a sash worn across the body

explanation.surface: A monarch is turned out in suitable attire for meeting a large crowd.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark covers the unstated garment: a royal sash is what a queen properly wears, and QU sits inside it to make SQUASH.
explanation.definitionFit: To squash people is to press them tightly together, which is what a crowd does to its members.

clue.text: Noise made by middle parts of mosques' swivel-chairs

indicators.note: the central parts of words are kept and their outer letters thrown away

blocks.note: the central three letters of a seven-letter word
the central four of twelve letters, ignoring the hyphen

explanation.surface: A creaking sound comes from the swivelling seats in the middle of some mosques.
explanation.walkthrough: The hyphenated word counts as one twelve-letter string, so its middle four letters straddle the hyphen.
explanation.definitionFit: A squelch is the wet sucking sound of feet in mud, a particular kind of noise.

clue.text: A case of dinner without having been properly introduced

definitions.note: the clue gives a case; the answer is the adjective naming one, as in upper case

indicators.note: with no proper introduction, the word lacks its opening letter

blocks.note: supper is an evening meal

explanation.surface: Someone turns up at a dinner party without anyone having introduced them to the guests.
explanation.walkthrough: SUPPER loses its first letter S. 'A case of' reads as an instance of something, but 'A case' is the definition: upper case is a case of lettering.
explanation.definitionFit: Printers keep capital letters in the upper case and small letters in the lower case, so upper names a case.

clue.text: Place for forger reserved in American university? On the contrary

indicators.note: one thing being in another means it sits inside it; the reversal of roles is signalled separately
this tells the solver to swap which piece holds and which is held

blocks.note: a reserved person is shy
the Massachusetts Institute of Technology

explanation.surface: Asks whether a forger's workplace is tucked away inside an American university.
explanation.walkthrough: Read literally the clue puts the reserved word inside the university; 'On the contrary' reverses which holds which. MIT is the Massachusetts Institute of Technology.
explanation.definitionFit: A smithy is a blacksmith's workshop, and a smith forges metal, so it is the forger's place of work.

clue.text: A flat, perhaps it once granted access to Number 10?

definitions.text: it once granted access to Number 10

blocks.note: first meaning: A-flat major is one example of a musical key

blocks.clueFragment: it once granted access to Number 10
blocks.note: second meaning: the door key of John Major, Prime Minister in the 1990s

explanation.surface: Wonders whether a mere flat once came with the key to Downing Street.
explanation.walkthrough: Number 10 Downing Street is the British Prime Minister's residence; John Major lived there from 1990 to 1997. 'A flat' looks like an apartment but is the musical note.
explanation.definitionFit: A-flat major is a tonality built on the note A-flat, so it is an instance of that kind of musical scale.

clue.text: Radiant silver luminance over town centre

indicators.note: the centre of a word is its middle letter, the one kept

blocks.note: Ag is the chemical symbol for silver
L is the symbol for luminance in physics
O is the cricket scoring abbreviation for an over
the middle letter of a five-letter word

explanation.surface: A town centre glows under shining silvery light.
explanation.walkthrough: Four short pieces line up in order; 'over' is the cricket term, an over being six balls bowled from one end.
explanation.definitionFit: Something aglow is glowing with light or colour, which is what radiant describes.

clue.text: Stay in glasses - the Italian's dressing

indicators.note: one piece being in another means it sits inside it

blocks.note: to live somewhere is to stay there
two round letters look like a pair of spectacles
il is Italian for the

explanation.surface: An Italian man keeps his spectacles on while getting dressed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Glasses' gives OO because the two letters look like a pair of lenses; 'dressing' looks like putting clothes on but is salad dressing.
explanation.definitionFit: Olive oil is a standard salad dressing, often used plain or mixed with vinegar.

clue.text: Match arranged between two Fords in Russian peninsula

indicators.note: to arrange is to set in a new order, so these letters get reordered
whatever goes between is flanked on both sides and so enclosed

blocks.note: the Ford Ka is a small car; two of them flank the middle
taken as written
the second of the two Ford Ka cars

explanation.surface: A football fixture is set up between two Ford teams in a Russian peninsula.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fords' are cars, not river crossings: the Ford Ka model appears twice, either side of the reworked letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Kamchatka is the large peninsula in Russia's far east, between the Sea of Okhotsk and the Pacific.

clue.text: Farm worker upturned cart and dung, spilling half

indicators.note: turning something up in a down clue flips its order bottom to top
losing half its contents means only part of the word remains

blocks.note: a dray is a low heavy cart, typically for barrels
manure is animal dung used as fertiliser

explanation.surface: A farmhand tips over a muck cart and loses half the load.
explanation.walkthrough: The first half of the six-letter fertiliser word survives; the rest is spilled.
explanation.definitionFit: A yardman is a labourer who works in a farmyard or stockyard, one sort of farm hand.

clue.text: Adult accepts punch, but not one hidden from audience

indicators.note: one is the letter I, and this says to leave it out
to accept something is to take it in, so one piece goes inside another

blocks.note: someone of age is legally an adult
a fist is a punch, as in a bunch of fives

explanation.surface: A grown-up takes a blow but no one in the theatre sees it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Adult' is a two-word phrase, and the punch sits between its words, splitting the phrase rather than wrapping it.
explanation.definitionFit: Offstage action happens out of sight of the audience, in the wings or behind the set.

clue.text: A loaf of bread in Lourdes cured flu without discomfort

indicators.note: Lourdes is a town in France, so the words are to be put into French
curing changes the state of something, so these letters are reworked

blocks.note: un pain is French for a loaf of bread
taken as written

explanation.surface: A miracle at the pilgrimage town of Lourdes: bread cures influenza painlessly.
explanation.walkthrough: Lourdes is a French pilgrimage site famed for healing, so 'cured' fits the picture while signalling the reworked letters; the French bread also looks like English pain.
explanation.definitionFit: Unpainful is a rare but valid adjective meaning causing no pain, the same as free from discomfort.

clue.text: Turkish city is no better than we’re told

indicators.note: being told something means hearing it spoken, so pronunciation is what counts

blocks.note: mere means no better than, as in a mere child

explanation.surface: A dismissive verdict on some Turkish city: it's not as good as people say.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Is mere' said quickly runs together into the city's name.
explanation.definitionFit: Izmir is a large port city on Turkey's Aegean coast, formerly called Smyrna.

clue.text: Dining occasions right for introduction of nutritious rolls

indicators.note: an introduction comes at the start, so the opening letter is kept
one thing for another means swapping it in as a replacement

blocks.note: lunches are midday meals
R is the abbreviation for right
the opening letter of the word

explanation.surface: Mealtimes are the right moment to bring in healthy bread rolls.
explanation.walkthrough: R replaces the N in LUNCHES. 'Rolls' looks like bread but is a verb, as a ship rolls and lurches.
explanation.definitionFit: A ship that lurches pitches or tilts suddenly, which is close to rolling from side to side.

clue.text: Welsh town in ruins, as reported by amateur

indicators.note: something reported is passed on by word of mouth, so only its sound counts

blocks.note: wrecks are ruins
a ham is an amateur, as in a radio ham or a ham actor

explanation.surface: A news item from an amateur reporter says a Welsh town has been laid waste.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In ruins' reads as a state but is taken as the noun wrecks. A ham is an amateur, especially a radio enthusiast.
explanation.definitionFit: Wrexham is a large town in north-east Wales, near the border with England.

clue.text: Religious duty enjoyed by justice

blocks.note: to have had something can mean to have enjoyed it
J is the abbreviation for Justice, a judge's title

explanation.surface: A judge takes pleasure in fulfilling a religious obligation.
explanation.walkthrough: J is the standard abbreviation for a judge styled Justice, as in Smith J.
explanation.definitionFit: The hadj (hajj) is the pilgrimage to Mecca that every able Muslim must make once, a pillar of Islam.

clue.text: Doctor prays team in capital get poorly coordinated

indicators.note: to doctor something is to tamper with it, so the letters are altered
pieces placed in another sit inside it

blocks.note: taken as written
a cricket or football team has eleven players, XI in Roman numerals
DC, the District of Columbia, is the US capital Washington

explanation.surface: A doctor prays that a team in the capital will be clumsy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Doctor' looks like a person praying but is a verb meaning tamper with. Washington DC supplies the outer letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Dyspraxia is a condition affecting motor coordination, so a dyspraxic person moves clumsily.

clue.text: Soldiers' kit is unreliable in January here in Central Asia

indicators.note: something unreliable cannot be trusted to stay put, so these letters move
a piece in another sits inside it

blocks.note: the TA is the Territorial Army, Britain's volunteer reserve
taken as written
the month cut to its first three letters, its usual short form

explanation.surface: Army equipment fails in the winter cold of a Central Asian posting.
explanation.walkthrough: TA stands for the Territorial Army, Britain's part-time reserve soldiers. The reworked letters go inside JAN.
explanation.definitionFit: Tajikistan is a mountainous former Soviet republic in Central Asia, so 'here' points to that place.

clue.text: Coolers in US eliminate fights

blocks.note: to ice someone is US slang for to kill them
a boxer fights in the ring

explanation.surface: American cooling-off periods put an end to brawls.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In US' does double duty: icebox is American English for a refrigerator, and ice for kill is US slang too.
explanation.definitionFit: Americans have long called a refrigerator an icebox, from the older insulated chest cooled by blocks of ice.

clue.text: Short, swelling song representing this country

indicators.note: something short is cut down, so the word loses its last letter

blocks.note: a bulge is a swelling
an aria is a solo song in opera

explanation.surface: A brief, rousing anthem standing for the nation.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Short, swelling song' reads as a crescendo anthem; the comma separates the trimming signal from its word.
explanation.definitionFit: Bulgaria is a Balkan country on the Black Sea; 'this country' simply names the answer as a nation.

clue.text: Theologian holding fixed equities could be made anxious

indicators.note: something fixed has been rigged or rearranged, so the letters are reordered
to hold is to grip around, so one piece wraps another

blocks.note: DD is a Doctor of Divinity
taken as written

explanation.surface: A churchman with a rigged stock portfolio might be worried.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fixed equities' sounds like fixed-income investments; 'fixed' is the signal to rearrange.
explanation.definitionFit: To disquiet is to make uneasy, so someone disquieted has been rendered worried and nervous.

clue.text: European opposing East Germany’s rising progress

indicators.note: in a down clue, rising reads from bottom to top, flipping the order

blocks.note: a Pole is a person from Poland
v. is short for versus, against
E is the compass abbreviation
D is the international vehicle code for Germany

explanation.surface: A European resisting East Germany's ascent in progress, a Cold War image.
explanation.walkthrough: 'East Germany' looks like one country but splits into two pieces, E and D, before the whole string flips.
explanation.definitionFit: To develop is to grow or advance, so as a verb it means the same as to progress.

clue.text: Originally just a snoring sound, making music of a sort

indicators.note: the origin of a word is its beginning, so opening letters are taken

blocks.note: the opening letter of each of the two words
zz is the comic-strip sound of snoring

explanation.surface: A mere snore turned out to be the start of a musical style.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Originally' seems to talk about history; it actually picks the first letters of the next two words.
explanation.definitionFit: Jazz is a genre of music born in New Orleans, so it is one sort of music.

clue.text: South Africa award Zulu second bit of finance for river

indicators.note: the second piece of a word is its second letter

blocks.note: ZA is the country code for South Africa
the MBE is a British honour, Member of the Order of the British Empire
Zulu is the radio alphabet word for Z
the second letter of the word

explanation.surface: South Africa gives a Zulu a grant of money for a river project.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Zulu' looks like a person but is the radio alphabet word for Z; the MBE is a British honour.
explanation.definitionFit: The Zambezi is the great southern African river that flows over Victoria Falls into the Indian Ocean.

clue.text: Work out for bust, waist and hips?

blocks.note: first meaning: to calculate or reckon
second meaning: the shape of a body, measured at those three points

explanation.walkthrough: 'Work out' suggests the gym, matching the body measurements, but it means calculate.
explanation.definitionFit: As a verb the word means to calculate, and as a noun it means body shape, judged by those three measurements.

clue.text: Sign over area with small dragons

indicators.note: something laid over another covers it, so one piece goes around the other

blocks.note: Virgo is a sign of the zodiac
A is the abbreviation for area
S is the clothing-size abbreviation for small

explanation.surface: A signpost over a patch of ground with little dragons on it, as on a map.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dragons' are not beasts here but fierce, domineering women.
explanation.definitionFit: A virago is a bad-tempered, overbearing woman, and dragon is an informal word for exactly that type.

clue.text: Bangladeshi Variety Shows/ Lord of the Dance

indicators.note: to show something is to put it on display, so the letters are there in plain view

blocks.note: spans the end of the first word and the start of the second

explanation.surface: Two show titles side by side: a Bangladeshi variety programme and the Irish dance spectacular Lord of the Dance.
explanation.walkthrough: The italics make both halves look like titles of stage shows, hiding that 'Shows' is the signal and the second title is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: In Hindu tradition Shiva as Nataraja is the cosmic dancer, the god called King or Lord of the Dance.

clue.text: Elliptical Roman poet’s clipped style

indicators.note: clipping trims the end off, so the last letter goes

blocks.note: Ovid was the Roman poet of the Metamorphoses
form can mean style or manner

explanation.surface: A Roman poet's terse, elliptical way of writing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Elliptical' suggests terse prose, matching 'clipped style', but it means oval-shaped.
explanation.definitionFit: Oviform means egg-shaped, from Latin ovum, and an egg's outline is roughly oval like an ellipse.

clue.text: Steer front of boat into kind of lake

blocks.note: a steer is a castrated bullock, a kind of ox
the bow is the forward end of a vessel

explanation.surface: Steering the prow of a boat out onto a lake.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Steer' reads as a verb about piloting but is the noun, a young bullock.
explanation.definitionFit: An oxbow lake is a curved lake left when a river meander is cut off from the main channel.

clue.text: Lined up entrances by golden temple in Egypt

indicators.note: an entrance is where you come in, so each word's first letter is taken

blocks.note: the opening letter of each word
by as in multiplied by, written as a times sign
or is gold in heraldry

explanation.surface: Visitors queue at the gates of a gilded Egyptian temple.
explanation.walkthrough: 'By' gives X as in three by four; OR is the heraldic word for gold.
explanation.definitionFit: Luxor Temple is the great ancient complex on the Nile's east bank at Thebes, in modern Egypt.

clue.text: Not even proficient after endless equine training

indicators.note: without an end, the word loses its final letter
training puts something into a new shape, so the letters are reworked
one piece placed after another simply follows it

blocks.note: the horsey adjective trimmed of its end
able means skilled or competent

explanation.surface: Someone who is not even competent after unending horse training.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Not even' looks like 'not even proficient' as a phrase, but stands alone as the definition. The trimmed word is reworked before the second piece follows.
explanation.definitionFit: Inequable means uneven or not uniform, the opposite of equable, so it means not even.

clue.text: Clear up impact of global warming on polar ice?

definitions.text: impact of global warming on polar ice

blocks.note: first meaning: to tidy things away

blocks.clueFragment: impact of global warming on polar ice
blocks.note: second meaning, cryptic: the floating sea ice called pack ice melts away

explanation.walkthrough: Pack ice is the mass of floating sea ice in polar waters; as it melts, the pack goes away, hence the question mark.
explanation.definitionFit: To pack away is to put things in their places, which is how you tidy a room.

clue.text: With AI, Chinese artist articulated methods

indicators.note: to articulate is to pronounce, so spoken sound is what counts

blocks.note: methods are ways, here two of them

explanation.surface: A Chinese artist explains his techniques with the help of artificial intelligence.
explanation.walkthrough: 'With AI' looks like artificial intelligence but is his first name: Ai Weiwei. The plural methods supply two ways.
explanation.definitionFit: Ai Weiwei is a celebrated Chinese contemporary artist and activist, so adding his first name identifies him.
